title: Personal Website
description: A personal project made to expand my skills in web development, also aiding in displaying my personal and professional life.
about: This project was created as a way to test my abilities and showcase my work and skills. I first built this website using raw HTML and CSS. After my first iteration, I migrated everything over to Svelte to increase the development speed. I chose to deploy to Cloudflare Workers for its built-in security, automatic scaling, cost effectiveness, and easy CI/CD GitHub integration.
lessons_learned: The biggest piece is that I learned how to use HTML and CSS on a much deeper level. It served me good doing research to find the best way to build this site without making it a big headache, considering I'm not a pro at coding. Migrating over to Svelte was a big time saver because it helped decrease duplicate code by writing reusable components.

title: IOT - Camera Monitor Security
description: A hands-on project aimed at evaluating the network security of low-cost camera monitors purchased from Amazon.
about: The goal of this project was to evaluate the security vulnerabilities of inexpensive camera monitors purchased from Amazon. Two cameras, each costing around $20, were set up following the included instructions to ensure a proper configuration. Once the cameras were connected to the network, we used a virtual machine running Wireshark on the same network to capture traffic. While signing into the cameras' mobile app and accessing the live feed, we analyzed the packets being transmitted. Our analysis revealed that both cameras transmitted usernames and passwords in plaintext, with no encryption in place, thus highlighting a critical security flaw
lessons_learned: The moral of the story was: Don't buy cheap security cameras. Security vulnerabilities in IOT devices can sometimes be undermined, and with this project we learned just how easy it can be to intercept credentials and gain unauthorized access. This was one of my first hands on experiences, and though it was small and in a controlled environment, it was very rewarding. Wireshark is one of my favorite tools

title: Wellmo - A Wellness App
description: A software engineering project aimed at finding the best software development life cycle for an app of our choosing.
about: This was a Software Engineering class project. We learned about the Software Development Life Cycles and how you can pick the one that best fits the category of your project. My team consisted of five, with myself being the team leader. We selected the Agile Model because it allowed us to split the project into three iterations which was useful for our timeframe, it allowed us to make changes as we kept moving forward, and increased accountability. Our app, WellMo, was created with the intention to help a user  keep track of their health related symptoms and other factors so they can report them to their doctor

title: RainCheck - A Weather App
description: An app created with a focus on human-computer interaction. What matters is how UI friendly it is for the users.
about: In human computer interaction class, we learn the value of making apps as user friendly as possible for your intended audience. In this project, no coding was involved, just a visual representation. As the team lead, I decided to create a weather app, but not your typical one. This project involved designing a visually engaging weather app focused on personalization and travel planning. The core idea was to allow users to create custom Bitmoji-style avatars dressed appropriately for different weather ranges. For example, users could assign outfits such as shorts and a tank top for 80-90°F weather or a raincoat and boots for rainy days. Once customized, the app's home screen would display the user's avatar alongside real-time weather and location data. Another key feature of the app was the Travel Calculator, which helped users plan trips based on weather preferences. Users could either search a specific location and view its typical weather by month or enter their preferred travel month, ideal weather conditions, or geographic setting to get destination recommendations. This project highlighted the importance of user-centered design, visual engagement, and practical functionality in developing intuitive interfaces
lessons_learned: Since this was a visual project, I learned how to use photoshop to get the Bitmoji avatar outlines and transfer them over to the project board, which was just in Google Slides

title: Office Statistics Dashboard
description: A visual of the office traffic received throughout the year. Data ranges from total visits to the average student GPA.
about: At work, I was responsible for maintaining our student and employee traffic data to support leadership in making strategic decisions. The data included in-person check-ins from our queue system, phone call logs, and daily email logs tracked by our student workers. This project was passed down to me, and while some visuals in Power BI were already built, each fiscal year (September 1 to August 31) requires a new dashboard. When it was my turn, I learned how to build the new dashboard on my own and even created new calculated columns in Power BI to capture additional insights.
lessons_learned: Although I inherited part of the setup, I figured out how to pull, clean, and organize the data myself which helped me understand the full process behind our reporting. There were a lot of other visuals I played around with such as what gender or College visits our office the most and for what types of services.
